solid.head: e9df87008285b25fc72d00c1e8f6d000193e013e
solid.review:
Independent re-review at e9df87008285b25fc72d00c1e8f6d000193e013e, against the previously reviewed e86f34d118b56d7e0d9405c5bdea7ba41ee989eb: the route-alias blocker is cleared. No new blocking source finding was identified.

I inspected all five corrected paths. The shared classifier mirrors the installed router's normalization, including static-segment case, end slashes and percent decoding. Server entry refuses every recognized noncanonical Telegram route before routing/rendering, scrubs its request event, and returns the private empty 404. Canonical probe routes retain the staging-origin, canonical-origin, expiry, hydration and asset-origin gates. Middleware now recognizes the same aliases through the shared classifier, including error responses. The existing Telegram linking routes receive the same protection.

I independently reran the original eight-URL control-flow reproduction with the exact fetched modules and their real dependency resolved in memory: all eight are recognized, production is refused, private classification applies and fixture callback values are removed. I also checked fifty spellings across the five Telegram routes against the installed router matcher and its comparablePath/decodeURI pipeline; classification and alias refusal agree. This reproducer is not a full SSR renderer or deployed Worker test. The added actual entry-server/middleware tests cover eleven aliases across six render contexts, canonical hydration/asset refusal and private render failures. The required native suites were run by hosted verify; I did not rerun the full native suites in this reviewer session.

All three applicable hosted checks are successful on this exact head: verify, Solid Doctor (PR) and storybook-audit. Solid Doctor (main) is skipped. Run: https://github.com/pirate-social-club/pirate-web-solid/actions/runs/38411407368 .

The cloud coordinator may now integrate this exact head with a normal merge through the authorized protected PR path, after fresh head/check/custody verification. This clears source acceptance; provider and staged serving acceptance are still open.

The probe module can precede the API migration: it reads the Solid Worker's same-origin public verification config and talks to Privy, without calling the api-next recovery, association, registration, guest or practice endpoints. For the proposed Solid-only Part A release, the operator must still establish the actual composed main and serving predecessor, preserved ingress/config references, current HNS guard and browser readiness, managed config/app binding, exact built artifact/version/readbacks and bounded recovery. Use the maintained guarded staging deploy from published main. Module independence does not waive whole-release compatibility or custody checks.

The phone return, cancellation and managed numeric-ID/subject/freshness lookup must complete before 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z. Browser observation alone remains insufficient account proof. PR604's provider and owner decisions remain pending and this review does not accept them.

contract.head: af4ac7d24985559ea2de611226f4860fdccfa67e
contract.review:
Independent draft review at af4ac7d24985559ea2de611226f4860fdccfa67e, document blob 4ab369e658ef00d6cd983d01fa9c644233fc6d3b.

The current revision preserves the accepted invariants: the same original promotable account and history, bot-local isolation, permanent historical practice-only attribution, one Telegram-ID association, independent numeric identity proof, and refusal instead of a merge or reassignment. It now makes protected explicit confirmation separate from verification in both flows, narrows the proposed limited session, and uses "Open my progress". These are useful corrections. The document correctly remains unaccepted and admits no implementation; provider choice and R1/R2/C1/E1 remain owner decision pending.

Two points still need clarification before this becomes an accepted implementation contract. Connect step4 currently combines linking a credential to a Privy user with writing the Pirate relation "atomically" under one lock. A PostgreSQL transaction cannot roll back a completed external provider link. The provider-specific successor must define the consented external mutation boundary, durable pending/uncertain states, same-target reconciliation and conflict refusal without moving a credential or silently authenticating another provider user. Distinguish provider login's permitted external identity creation from the no-Pirate-mutation guarantee after cancellation. Do not promise cross-system atomicity.

For the limited session, specify a distinct declarative principal/capability that cannot satisfy ordinary user authority, rather than an ad hoc route allowlist. The current operation list is a good semantic boundary, but the generated auth policy and default refusal must enforce it. C1 should say the relation grants exactly the reviewed read-only projection instead of both granting a projection and saying it grants no new authority. Also make clear whether linking Telegram adds a future full-account login method or only the history relation: those are different effects needing explicit consent. A provider subject already mapped elsewhere must require independent sign-in and confirmation of the target; routing to Connect is not account proof.

The workspace_owner's reply asked what the specs and research recommend; it did not approve the four decisions. My recommendation is limited practice access first, the existing practice-only restriction, a private read-only relation with new bot lessons continuing the original practice profile, and one "Open my progress" action. The research offers limited or full recovery; limited first is a reviewer recommendation, not an already ratified requirement. Keep owner decision pending until an explicit choice is recorded.

Solid64 source is cleared at e9df8700, all three applicable checks pass, and its normal merge is verified as b835c734d019b5523ccbd53aa74251f51c27beb5. The probe module can precede the API migration, subject to whole-release guarded staging checks and actual serving/config/resource custody. Real phone and managed provider evidence remain open. This draft review does not select Privy, activate a completion button, authorize implementation or replace reviewed control-plane integration.
